label: Morning Brief
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Artificial-intelligence stocks continued to weaken globally as investors digested the Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections (WSJ, 4:46 AM ET). Treasury and European bond yields fell, with U.S. yields at eight-week lows, as markets weighed the prospect of fiscal restraint under a divided government (WSJ, 5:15 AM ET). Chipmaker Qualcomm's earnings disappointed (WSJ). Bloomberg reported that large hyperscaler tech stocks rose as Democrats threaten to slow AI spending, though not all AI companies fared well. Bloomberg also reported that Hong Kong stocks are rebounding as investors rotate from hardware stocks into discounted Chinese internet platforms. Oil rose but stayed below $100 a barrel as traders weighed U.S.-Iran diplomacy (WSJ, 5:38 AM ET), after plunging on Wednesday as the Dow posted its best day in 18 months (MarketWatch).
